newsitem.title: USA: Moody's upgrades Detroit sewer revenue bonds to A1.
newsitem.headline: Moody's upgrades Detroit sewer revenue bonds to A1.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service announced Friday it has upgraded the bonded debt of the Detroit regional sewer system to A1 from A in conjunction with the expected sale of $275.225 million of Series 1997A sewer revenue bonds next week.
MBIA is expected to insure the bonds expected to be sold Tuesday, subject to review, with the underlying rating maintained with a stable outlook, Moody's said.
"The system has benefited from its broad service area as population and customer losses in Detroit have resulted in gains within the suburban base," Moody's said.
Moody's said an increasingly diversified area economy in recent years with large growth in service industries outside Detroit has benefited the system.
Corporate restructuring and reinvestment has also minimized the economic impact of the still cyclical automobile industry in the region as well, Moody's said.
"Further, Moody's believes that an overall increase in economic activity within Detroit bodes well for continued stabilization of the service area," Moody's said.

Detroit's capital improvement program through 2002 outlines a need for approximately $1 billion, including $715 million expected to be financed through additional sewer revenue bond offerings, Moody's said.
Moody's expects that substantial debt will continue to be manageable, however, because the low current sewer rates provide some flexibility for future increases to support the debt.
